title: Polylogarithmic updates for the exact arboricity value
formal: Can exact integral arboricity of a fully dynamic simple graph be maintained deterministically in polylogarithmic amortized update time with constant-time value queries?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with words of Θ(log(n+2)) bits, unit-cost word arithmetic, Boolean operations, shifts, comparisons and memory accesses, and no nonuniform advice. Constants may be enlarged to address the stated space. The vertex set [n] is fixed, graphs are simple and undirected, and updates insert an absent edge or delete a present edge. Unless stated otherwise the graph starts empty; all outputs must be correct for every legal update sequence. The arboricity a(G) is the smallest integer a≥0 such that E can be partitioned into a forests, where a forest is an acyclic undirected graph on V; the empty graph has arboricity zero. The structure reports only this integer and need not provide a forest partition or orientation. Require O(n log^c(n+2)) initialization on the empty graph, O((n+m)log^c(n+2)) words of space at current edge count m, O(log^c(n+2)) amortized update time and O(1) worst-case query time, for an absolute c. For U updates and Q queries, the total time after initialization is O(U log^c(n+2)+Q). No bound on arboricity is promised and its numeric value may grow with n.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of the specified correctness and resource guarantees, or prove that this precise target is impossible. Any conditional impossibility must explicitly state its hypothesis and the implication proved. Approximation or a bound polynomial in current arboricity does not meet this target. A lower bound that only concerns explicit forest decompositions must not be transferred to value-only queries.
context: The tree-packing paper obtains approximation results, including polylogarithmic randomized updates for fractional arboricity. Those guarantees do not give the exact integer value with the resources requested here.
why: Value-only maintenance separates the intrinsic difficulty of arboricity from the cost of explicitly changing a forest decomposition.

import_provenance.original_title: Polylogarithmic updates for the exact arboricity value
import_provenance.original_statement: Can the exact arboricity of a fully dynamic undirected graph—the minimum number of forests covering its edges—be maintained with polylogarithmic amortized update time and constant-time value queries? This is an editorial target extending Saurabh and coauthors’ exact-maintenance work; it asks only for the value, not explicit maintenance of an optimal forest decomposition.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Known near-optimal approximation structures do not give the exact value. Lower bounds for explicitly changing an optimal forest decomposition do not by themselves rule out the value-only target.

context_blocks.text: The tree-packing paper obtains approximation results, including polylogarithmic randomized updates for fractional arboricity. Those guarantees do not give the exact integer value with the resources requested here.

sentences: Arboricity is the minimum number of forests covering the edges without overlap.
The structure reports that integer exactly.
The graph can pass through arbitrary arboricity values.
Only a value query is required, not an explicit forest partition.
The selected target is deterministic polylogarithmic amortized update time.
